description: A ground-level photograph depicts a forest landscape severely impacted by environmental damage, characterised by numerous dead, standing trees. The trees are tall, bare, and greyish, appearing stripped of all foliage, indicative of extensive forest dieback. The ground is covered with dry, yellowish-brown grass and sparse, small green bushes or saplings, suggesting limited new growth or understory vegetation. The sky is overcast and light grey. This image exemplifies a "Damaged forest" as defined in Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) documentation, where damage is visible through discolouration (lack of leaves/needles) due to factors such as pests (e.g., bark-beetle attacks), storm events, or other environmental stressors. The visible trees are indicative of monocultures, which the surrounding text describes as more vulnerable.
